title: KV resilience blueprint & probing matrix for cost-aware TTLs and batch-sensitive keys
creator: Marco Rivera
description: Create a reproducible 'resilience blueprint' and probing matrix to generate safe, automated recommendations for KV/prefix caching. Deliverables: (1) hit-rate modeling that ties to economic impact (tokens saved / $), (2) TTL tier suggestions that are batch-aware and cascade safely across prefixes, and (3) guidance + config generator for cache key design that reduces collision and preserves batching efficiency. Emphasize staged apply/rollback automation: dry-run simulations, shadowing, canary, and automated conservative rollback triggers.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible hit-rate simulator that accepts production prefix histograms and emits expected token-savings and latency delta estimates
A TTL recommendation output that lists per-prefix TTL tiers and confidence bands (low/medium/high) and a suggested staged rollout plan
A cache-key checklist + automated linter that flags high-collision patterns and batch-unfriendly key shapes
A safe-apply harness that can run dry-run -> shadow -> canary -> gradual rollout with automatic rollback on defined SLO regressions
Benchmarks showing >= 10% net token-cost reduction on two sampled customer workloads without breaking 99th pct latency SLO
implementation_plan: 1) Telemetry injection: ensure prefix-level request distribution, sequence-length buckets, and batching footprint are exportable from runtime (work with telemetry infra)
2) Probe harness: build synthetic traffic generator that can replay real prefix distributions with configurable batching params and optional jitter
3) Hit-rate model: implement a hybrid analytical + ML model that predicts hit probability under cascading TTL tiers and given batching window sizes
4) Policy synthesizer: convert hit-rate outputs into TTL tier proposals with confidence bands and cost-benefit ranking
5) Key-shape linter: static analyzer for upstream SDKs and routing rules to detect high-variance key components that harm cache reuse
6) Safe-apply orchestration: integrate with rollout service to support dry-run (shadow), canary cohort selection, SLA monitors, and auto-revert hooks
7) Dashboarding: add per-rollout telemetry (tokens saved, p95 latency, error-rate, rollback reason) in Console for engineers and PMs
8) Docs & runbooks: author operator playbook for manual intervention scenarios and postmortem templates
testing_plan: Unit tests for hit-model math and edge cases (zero-traffic prefixes, heavy-tail distributions)
End-to-end replay tests against three synthetic workloads (PLG chat, high-throughput embedding, enterprise long-request sequences)
Shadow deploys to simulate TTL tiers without affecting production caches, measure expected hit uplift and false-positives
Canary rollout to 1% tenants with automated SLO gates (p95 latency, token cost, error-rate) and manual approval step for 10%+ expansion
Chaos tests: simulate KV eviction storms, cache node restarts, and synthetic hot-prefix surges to validate safe-apply guardrails
rollback_plan: Automatic rollback triggers: p95 latency regression > 10% vs baseline OR error-rate increase > 0.5% OR token-savings negative for two consecutive 10-minute windows
Manual rollback steps: (a) abort rollout in console, (b) reapply previous TTL config, (c) run quick verification replay for impacted prefixes, (d) open postmortem ticket and attach probe logs
Rollback safety: all TTL changes are applied as additive shadow policies first (no eviction), followed by staged TTL enforcement to prevent sudden mass-evictions
Fallback plan: if config reapply fails, route affected traffic to compatible model variant with disabled caching for safety until root cause is resolved
metrics: Primary: estimated tokens saved per 1M requests (simulation and observed)
Primary: $ saved per 1M requests (based on per-token unit economics)
SLOs: p95 latency delta (ms) during rollout and steady-state
Secondary: observed prefix hit-rate delta, collision rate (unique keys / requests), eviction storms frequency
Safety: rollout rollback count and time-to-recover
